text: As a user, I want the login page to be fast and user-friendly.

findings.label: confirmed
findings.evidence: Matched vague adjective "fast" (rule R-AMB-01: subjective quality word without a measurable threshold).
findings.justification: "Fast" has no unit or target, so two developers could build very different pages and both claim the story is done.

findings.label: confirmed
findings.evidence: Matched vague adjective "user-friendly" (rule R-AMB-01: subjective quality word without a measurable threshold).
findings.justification: "User-friendly" is subjective; it is unclear which user group or which usability criteria apply.

findings.label: AI only
findings.evidence: No rule matched this span. Flagged by the language model in 3 of 5 runs.
findings.justification: Neither quality can be tested as written, because there is no pass/fail condition for a tester to check.

findings.span_text: I want the login page to be fast and user-friendly
findings.label: rule only
findings.evidence: No "so that ..." benefit clause found (rule R-BV-01: story ends without a stated purpose).

findings.label: possible issue
findings.evidence: No rule matched this span. Flagged by the language model in 1 of 5 runs.
findings.justification: It might be unclear which login method (password, SSO) and which error cases the page must cover.

improved.text: As a registered customer, I want the login page to load in [under 2 seconds] on [a typical broadband connection] so that I can start my task without waiting.
improved.acceptance_criteria_gherkin:
Feature: Login page performance
  Scenario: Login page loads quickly
    Given the login page is requested over [a typical broadband connection]
    When the user opens the login page
    Then the form is fully displayed within [2 seconds]
    And the username field has keyboard focus

  Scenario: Login form is operable by keyboard
    Given the login page is displayed
    When the user presses Tab
    Then the focus moves to the next form control
assumptions: "Fast" is interpreted as a 95th-percentile load time of under 2 seconds.
A typical broadband connection means at least 10 Mbit/s.
"User-friendly" is narrowed to keyboard operability; further usability criteria need a separate story.

text: As an admin, I want to export reports and manage users and send notifications so that the team stays informed.

findings.span_text: export reports and manage users and send notifications
findings.label: confirmed
findings.evidence: Matched 2 coordinating conjunctions "and" joining 3 verb phrases (rule R-ATOM-01: multiple actions in one story).
findings.justification: Exporting, user management and notifications are three separate capabilities and should be split into three stories.

findings.label: AI only
findings.evidence: No rule matched this span. Flagged by the language model in 3 of 5 runs.
findings.justification: There is no observable outcome that shows the team is informed, so the benefit cannot be verified.

findings.label: possible issue
findings.evidence: No rule matched this span. Flagged by the language model in 1 of 5 runs.
findings.justification: The report types and export format are not mentioned.

improved.text: As an admin, I want to export the monthly usage report as [a CSV file] so that the team can review usage figures.
improved.acceptance_criteria_gherkin:
Feature: Export monthly usage report
  Scenario: Admin exports the report
    Given an admin is signed in
    And usage data exists for [the previous calendar month]
    When the admin selects "Export CSV"
    Then a CSV file with one row per user is downloaded
assumptions: Only the monthly usage report is in scope; user management and notifications become separate stories.
CSV is the only required export format.

improved.text: As a returning customer, I want to see a list of my orders from the last [12 months] so that I can check what I have already bought.
improved.acceptance_criteria_gherkin:
Feature: Order history
  Scenario: Customer views past orders
    Given a signed-in customer with orders in the last [12 months]
    When the customer opens "My orders"
    Then the orders are listed newest first
    And each entry shows the order date and [the order total]
assumptions: Order history covers the last 12 months only.
Each entry shows the order date and total; item-level detail is out of scope.

text: As a librarian, I want to receive an email when a reserved book is returned so that I can collect it promptly.

findings.label: confirmed
findings.evidence: Matched vague adverb "promptly" (rule R-AMB-02: time expression without a measurable limit).
findings.justification: "Promptly" does not say how soon the email must arrive or how long the book is held.

findings.label: possible issue
